2611.13034.image_caption: Figure 1 : From fixed practice to adversarial co-evolution. (a) Fixed practice improves execution against an unchanged challenge source. (b) In RoboACE, the curriculum exposes current execution weaknesses, while execution expands its capabilities through reusable harness revisions. As capabilities grow, the curriculum targets new weaknesses, sustaining adversarial co-evolution. The blue and orange robots represent the execution and curriculum harnesses, respectively.

2611.13713.image_caption: Figure 1. Three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization. Realistic benchmarking establishes evaluation settings, tool-grounded agents optimize RTL beyond synthesis, and synthesis optimization extends agentic search from flow tuning to algorithm discovery.

2611.14017.image_caption: Figure 1. Long-horizon memory learning involves multiple updates but only a terminal QA reward, making fine-grained credit assignment difficult. Hand-crafted methods use fixed, non-personalized rules, while RL-based methods rely on sparse scalar feedback with ambiguous step/token attribution. PMR decouples direction from magnitude : the QA advantage determines the learning direction, while personalized rubric evidence modulates credit magnitude through direction-safe gating.

2611.14019.image_caption: Figure 1: Comparison between vanilla text-only skill-based agents and the PASE framework.

2611.14326.image_caption: Figure 1: A locally useful episode-derived lesson may overgeneralize or regress archived skills if directly written into memory. FGSE tests each lesson as a structured hypothesis in a temporary state and commits only verified, transferable updates to long-term memory.

2611.12933.image_caption: Figure 1: Directed communication graph during an autonomous experiment ( Exp3 ). Edge labels give message counts and edge width indicates message volume, reflecting coordination and human involvement within the multi-agent system. The gray band is the closed loop of acquisition (Bluesky), analysis (SciAnalysis) and steering (gpCAM). Right: the initial exchange of a session. Bottom: schematic of the 11-BM Complex Materials Scattering (CMS) beamline at the National Synchrotron Light Source II (NSLS-II).

2611.12954.image_caption: Figure 1: Conceptual comparison between (a) conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and (b) the proposed Physics2Weight (PtW). PINNs optimize neural network weights by minimizing physics-informed loss functions, whereas PtW edits architectures and directly generates weights from governing equations and initial and boundary conditions using an LLM, without gradient-based optimization.

2611.12958.image_caption: Figure 1. The Evolution of Self-Driving Laboratories. This timeline traces the development of autonomous experimentation systems from initial concepts in the 1940s to foundation model integration in recent years, spanning three eras: Early Era (1940s–2009, bottom) establishing foundational principles from design of experiments to closed-loop robot scientist; Modern Era (2009–2022, middle) deploying specialised robotic platforms across scientific domains; and LLMs Era (2022–present, top) integrating foundation models for high-level reasoning.

2611.13329.image_caption: Figure 1: Workflow for agent-guided exchange–correlation functional discovery and evaluation. (a) A coordinator and thematic agent islands generate executable proposals, drawing on shared plans, lineages, results, and summaries. (b) The MCP server connects agents to the GPU evaluator, which fits coefficients on training data, measures validation WRMSD, and applies four screening checks: spin interchange, the uniform-gas exchange limit, exchange-factor scaling, and grid sensitivity. (c) Selected candidates and fitted parameters are frozen before held-out MGCDB84 testing, selected self-consistent-field validation, and external evaluation on the 36-dataset computational subset of GSCDB137. These downstream assessments are separate from discovery; their results were not used to fit, rank, or select candidates.

2611.13410.image_caption: Figure 2 : One training cycle of SteerDistill. (i) Closed-loop teacher steering guides the frozen student to revise divergent turns and uses execution feedback to refine the guidance. Local verification compares the resulting environment transition with that of a successful teacher reference. On failure, the student retries with refined guidance from the same pre-error history and state. Verified corrections are retained, and rollout continues without guidance. (ii) To internalize these corrections, the learner receives no guidance and learns from the steered snapshot’s predictions at corrected turns and the full-precision teacher’s predictions elsewhere. Context c c contains the retained history and response prefix without steering prompts; only the steered target additionally receives G G . The updated student generates the next cycle’s rollouts.

2611.13627.image_caption: Figure 2: Comparison of dependency-unaware (top) and dependency-aware (bottom) diagnostics.

2611.13758.image_caption: Fig. 1: System diagram, showing experiment 5 in this study. A TinyEEGNet network, with all its weights initialized to 0, is written through the reasoning of Claude Opus 5.5 using only 5 training subjects, and matches the same network trained by gradient descent on 30 training subjects.

2611.14009.image_caption: Figure 4 : A Visual episode continues from its own saved file. We follow one episode from a late training update on the fitness-product showcase task. In (a) the student writes down what is wrong with the page and how it will rewrite it, before its context is replaced. In (b) it lists the workspace afterwards and reads that note back. In (c) it delivers a page that carries the sections the note listed.

2611.14320.image_caption: Figure 1: Memory-induced degradation and WikiTrace. (a) The agent solves a task without memory but fails with memory that holds a wrong insight. (b) With WikiTrace, the agent follows the wrong insight’s links to its source run, revises it, and solves the task.

2611.14356.image_caption: Figure 1. Position and workflow of EngineAgent: agentically mapping rapidly evolving LLM architectures onto heterogeneous mobile hardware for inference engines.

2611.14514.image_caption: Figure 1 : A contrast set turns a rejection into a resolution. A hypothesis generator proposes a contrast set of three competing explanations ( H 1 H_{1} – H 3 H_{3} ) for how X relates to Y, and coder, analyst, reviewer, and reviser agents run an experiment that produces evidence. Bars show elicited belief in each explanation before and after the same evidence. Contrastive Discovery updates belief over all three explanations and moves the lead from H 1 H_{1} (0.64) to H 2 H_{2} (0.81), so the question resolves to H 2 H_{2} and H 1 H_{1} is ruled out. Pointwise discovery updates belief only in H 1 H_{1} (0.64 to 0.07), so it records a rejection but leaves the question unresolved. See § 3 and § 4 for details.

2611.12988.image_caption: Figure 3: Role-wise continuation changes, in percentage points. Target and OOD losses dominate in the backbones with the largest mean declines. Colors show descriptive means, not significance.

2611.13218.image_caption: Figure 1: The environment and the mechanism. Left: the N = 64 N=64 prompts, colored by whether the verifier accepts a designated wrong answer h h ; every prompt accepts exactly one wrong string, so sweeping u = m / N u=m/N leaves the static false-positive rate unchanged. Center and right: with shared parameters every prompt’s gradient lands on the same weights, so h h is pushed up by the prompts that accept it and down by those that reject it (Lemma 1 ); with per-prompt parameters the cross-prompt term is identically zero (Corollary 1 ).

2611.13367.image_caption: Figure 1: (a) The setting. An assistant submits a plan p p (a program); the gatekeeper consults two rulebooks, one permissive and one prohibitive, each of which accepts only finite, mechanically checkable evidence: a receipt (a certificate). The gatekeeper admits p p when a permission receipt is found, rejects it when a prohibition receipt is found, and otherwise can only keep searching. (b) Why the permissive rulebook cannot be complete. The plan “solve this puzzle, then open the safe” ( p e , w p_{e,w} , which simulates a machine M e M_{e} on input w w and opens the safe only if the simulation halts) is safe exactly when the puzzle has no solution. A permission receipt for it would be a receipt that the kettle never boils, that is, that M e ​ ( w ) M_{e}(w) never halts, and no rulebook can issue such receipts for every non-halting computation (Lemma 2.3 ). (c) A concrete instance. The plan that searches even numbers for one that is not a sum of two primes and opens the safe only if it finds one is safe exactly when Goldbach’s conjecture is true. Bounded tests of 10 10 to 10 6 10^{6} steps all permit it (Section 6 ); no gatekeeper on Earth can currently certify it.

2611.13994.image_caption: Figure 2: Capability of agent configurations on the final release. a , Mean score over the 64 tasks for each of the 22 configurations (bars; the axis starts at 25), with 95% bootstrap CIs over tasks (5,000 resamples); failed tasks score 0 and their count is given next to the interval. Dotted line, the best mean. The two columns to the right give the agent wall-clock time summed over the 64 tasks and the input (bar) and output (small number) tokens in millions; input includes cached prompt tokens. Colour marks the backbone (one colour family per vendor, the newer backbone darker). b , Domain means per configuration, rows ordered as in a ( n = 8 n=8 tasks per domain). c , Scaffold–backbone design: mean score of four model-agnostic scaffolds with four backbones, with row and column means. d , Vendor-CLI design: each coding CLI with the older and the newer of its vendor’s two backbones (arrow), and OpenCode with the newer backbone (open diamond). e , Agent wall-clock time against mean score; red, the search-based MLEvolve scaffold.
